chosen.premise: Beedrill has three poison barbs, but its tail barb secretes its most powerful poison.
chosen.hook: Beedrill has three stingers—but one is the worst.
chosen.visualIdea: Three stingers receive on-screen labels; the tail stinger gets a pulsing venom meter that maxes out.
chosen.note: A sharply Beedrill-specific contradiction: three poison barbs, but the tail barb is the most dangerous. The Pokédex directly supports it and the venom-meter visual is immediate.

candidates.premise: Weedle becomes Kakuna at level 7, then just three levels later evolves into Beedrill.
candidates.hook: This Pokémon's cocoon phase lasts only three levels.
candidates.visualIdea: A level counter climbs from 7 to 10 while Kakuna's shell cracks into Beedrill in three rapid beats.
candidates.note: The three-level Kakuna window is concrete and highly visual. It is compelling, though its surprise depends on the audience knowing the evolution chain and the cited levels come from secondary data.

candidates.premise: Mega Beedrill is 0.4 meters taller and 11 kilograms heavier than Beedrill.
candidates.visualIdea: Regular and Mega Beedrill stand on a height chart and scales as +0.4 m and +11 kg snap onscreen.
candidates.note: The comparison is precise and fully supported, but Mega stat differences are less inherently surprising than Beedrill's venom hierarchy.

candidates.premise: Beedrill defeats prey with poisonous stings, then carries the victim back to its nest for food.
candidates.hook: Beedrill doesn't just sting prey—it takes it home.
candidates.visualIdea: A sharp three-step sequence: high-speed sting, prey silhouette, then Beedrill flying toward a guarded nest.
candidates.note: Very distinctive and unsettling: Beedrill takes defeated prey home. The Pokédex supports the sequence, though carrying the victim is slightly more interpretive than the other wording.

candidates.premise: Beedrill's best attack is a high-speed loop: strike with poison needles, then fly away.
candidates.hook: Beedrill's best move is: sting, vanish, repeat.
candidates.visualIdea: A looping flight trail circles a target as Beedrill darts in, lands poison hits, and exits at speed.
candidates.note: Strongly supported and easy to animate, but the sting-and-retreat behavior feels more like a combat tactic than a surprising Beedrill revelation.

candidates.premise: Approaching a Beedrill nest can trigger a furious swarm because Beedrill is extremely territorial.
candidates.hook: The one place you should never go near: a Beedrill nest.
candidates.visualIdea: A camera creeps toward a nest; one Beedrill becomes a darkening swarm racing straight at the lens.
candidates.note: The swarm escalation is well supported, but territorial nest defense is a broadly expected bee-like trait and the premise lacks a distinctive rule or number.
